```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

noqtis brings post-quantum signatures (ML-DSA, SLH-DSA), key
encapsulation (ML-KEM, HQC) and hashes to R, through a bundled C library.
Keys, signatures and ciphertexts are raw vectors in the encodings the
standards define.

```{r}
library(noqtis)
head(nqalgs())
```

## Signing

```{r}
k <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-65")
sig <- nqsign(k$sk, "the results in table 2", "ML-DSA-65")
length(sig)
nqverify(k$pk, "the results in table 2", sig, "ML-DSA-65")
nqverify(k$pk, "the results in table 3", sig, "ML-DSA-65")
```

A context string binds a signature to one use; verification needs the
same context.

```{r}
sig <- nqsign(k$sk, "data", "ML-DSA-65", ctx = "analysis-v1")
nqverify(k$pk, "data", sig, "ML-DSA-65", ctx = "analysis-v1")
nqverify(k$pk, "data", sig, "ML-DSA-65")
```

## Key encapsulation

```{r}
k <- nqkeygen("ML-KEM-768")
e <- nqencap(k$pk, "ML-KEM-768")
identical(nqdecap(k$sk, e$ct, "ML-KEM-768"), e$ss)
```

## Hashes

```{r}
nqhash("abc", hex = TRUE)
nqhash("abc", "sha3-256", hex = TRUE)
```

## Capsules

A capsule is a signed record of the exact files in a folder. Seal it once,
and anyone with the public key can check later that no file was changed,
added or removed.

```{r}
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "analysis")
dir.create(d)
writeLines(c("x,y", "1,2"), file.path(d, "data.csv"))
k <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-44")
nqseal(d, k$sk, k$pk, "ML-DSA-44", meta = '{"project":"vignette"}')
nqcheck(d, k$pk)

writeLines(c("x,y", "1,3"), file.path(d, "data.csv"))
r <- nqcheck(d, k$pk)
r[!r$ok, ]
```

The package ships a capsule made by the noqtis library's own tests:

```{r}
g <- system.file("extdata", "capsule", package = "noqtis")
attr(nqcheck(g), "ok")
```

A format 2 capsule can also prove single files to a reader who should not
see the others, and records the capsules it was made from:

```{r}
d2 <- file.path(tempdir(), "model")
dir.create(d2)
writeLines("coef,0.4", file.path(d2, "fit.csv"))
writeLines("private", file.path(d2, "notes.txt"))
nqseal(d2, k$sk, k$pk, "ML-DSA-44", inputs = c(raw = g))
p <- nqprove(d2, "fit.csv")
attr(nqcheck(NULL, k$pk, proof = p), "ok")
attr(nqcheck(d2, k$pk, lineage = g), "ok")
```

`nqrotate()` and `nqrevoke()` write key statements that `nqcheck(keys = )`
follows, and `nqdsse()` signs a DSSE envelope, the wrapper in-toto and
SLSA use.

## Randomness

Key generation, signing and encapsulation take their randomness from the
operating system (`getrandom()`, `arc4random_buf()` or
`BCryptGenRandom()`), never from R's generator: `set.seed()` does not
make them repeat. For test vectors, `nqkeygen()` and `nqencap()` take an
explicit `seed`, and `nqsign()` has `det = TRUE`.
